sources.title: Tamberlin opens an online order portal for business customers

company_claims.text: Tamberlin Print & Mail is a family-owned commercial printing and direct-mail company in Dayton, Ohio, founded in 1987, with 45 employees.
Tamberlin prints and mails catalogs, statements and postcards for regional banks, hospitals and retailers.

Tamberlin opened an online order portal in February 2026; orders arriving by email are still entered by hand by customer service, and the company plans to connect both channels to the production schedule by mid-2027.

The role is the first in-house software engineer, reporting to the Operations Director: it covers automating order intake from email and the portal into the production schedule, building internal reports, maintaining the portal's integrations, and supporting colleagues who use these tools every day.
The role likely exists to connect email and portal orders to the production schedule by mid-2027.

company_profile.note: first in-house engineer; documented trigger is the email/portal order-intake plan

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role at Tamberlin Print & Mail. Your news on the online order portal says that orders arriving by email are still entered by hand, and that you plan to connect both channels to the production schedule by mid-2027. The posting makes this role your first in-house software engineer, with order intake listed first among its responsibilities.

At Northbridge Public Library I wrote a Python script that automated the weekly public-computer reservation report, which had been compiled by hand in a spreadsheet. My supervisor estimated about two hours of staff time saved per week. I also resolved device and account issues for library staff and patrons, the kind of day-to-day support the posting describes for colleagues who use these tools.

My largest project is RouteWise, a capstone built by a team of three. I owned its backend, a FastAPI service with REST endpoints over PostgreSQL, covered by pytest tests. Four volunteer coordinators used it in a three-week pilot, and in a survey they said planning time per shift fell from about twenty-five minutes to about ten.

I have not used Microsoft Power Automate, which the posting lists as preferred. My closest experience is scripting: the reservation script replaced a hand-compiled report, and RouteWise groups delivery stops into routes, work the coordinators had done by hand. I would learn Power Automate on one small intake task and test the flow before anyone relies on it.

If this role exists mainly to connect email and portal orders to the production schedule by mid-2027, I would start with that intake work. I would welcome a conversation about which step you need automated first.

interview.question: How would you start on the order intake that still runs by hand?
interview.talking_points: Email orders are still entered by hand and the plan is to connect both channels by mid-2027. I have not built an intake flow. Start by mapping one email order to the production-schedule fields, then script the repetitive step, as I did for the reservation report.

interview.question: Which preferred skill in the posting do you lack, and how would you close the gap?
interview.talking_points: Microsoft's automation tool, which I have not used. Nearest evidence: the scripted reservation report and the REST endpoints in RouteWise. Ramp-up: learn it on one small intake task and test the flow before anyone relies on it.

questions.ask: Have you used Power Automate or another workflow tool (Zapier, Power Apps, n8n) anywhere?
questions.why: R5 is a declared gap; any workflow-tool use would be nearer evidence than scripting.

questions.ask: Are you looking for a full-time role, from which date, and can you work on site in Dayton, OH?
questions.why: Your documents state January 2027 and a move to Lyon only.
